title: iPhone Safari CSP allows Apple Music HLS audio
acceptance: The page CSP in apps/web/public/_headers lists https://*.itunes.apple.com in media-src, matching connect-src, so iPhone Safari's <audio> element may load Apple's HLS manifest (aod-ssl.itunes.apple.com).
The _headers comment explains why media-src needs the host on iOS (native HLS) and not on desktop (MSE blob:).
No other directive changes; provider audio is still served by Apple to the official MusicKit player (no proxy, cache or derivation).

evidence.summary: Owner iPhone Safari with Mac Web Inspector, 2026-10-28, production Worker d092af3c-114f-416f-bbe5-cb112cb52306, bundle assets/index-BTdVQWvK.js. Console: 'Refused to load https://aod-ssl.itunes.apple.com/.../mzaf_A1440754477...m3u8 because it does not appear in the media-src directive of the Content Security Policy', then MusicKit mediaPlaybackError MEDIA_PLAYBACK 'Playback Error'. setQueue for song 1440754477 timed out (20 s, twice) without an emulated user gesture and resolved in 313 ms with one.
Adds https://*.itunes.apple.com to media-src in apps/web/public/_headers. Owner-gated (security headers).

resolution: media-src now allows https://*.itunes.apple.com. Whether iPhone Safari plays audibly is verified separately in RF-29 after an owner deploy.
